dense_backbone.method: fixed robust endpoint persistence from released dense prefix pseudo-tracks
dense_backbone.selection: none; all settings fixed before future source outcomes

arms.tapnext_direct: dense persistence plus robust sparse correction at geometry-MAP nodes
arms.tapnext_graph: dense persistence plus the same sparse correction smoothed on the PhysTwin spring graph

predictive_uq.future_rule: posterior discrepancy variance plus random-walk growth by elapsed frames
predictive_uq.coverage_scope: conditional isotropic graph-node discrepancy intervals; calibration not assumed

information_boundary.provider_inputs: sealed causal RGB-D prefix predictions from the passed eight-case transfer study
information_boundary.dense_inputs: released object pseudo-tracks strictly before each training boundary
information_boundary.association: candidate probabilities use query-frame geometry only
information_boundary.prior_reliability: provider confidence, mask/depth quality, carrier disagreement, and assignment entropy; never physical innovation
information_boundary.innovation: processed once by a reliability-conditioned robust mixture likelihood
information_boundary.future_prediction: physical rollout plus frozen discrepancy fields; no future real observation
information_boundary.future_evaluation: staged source future opened only after each prediction seal

advancement_rule: Proceed to an independently preregistered fresh-object evaluation only if every documented accuracy, hidden-transfer, fallback, support, and calibration gate passes.
claim_boundary: Eight-case opened-source Bayesian-PhysTwin assimilation study. It tests whether a sealed TAPNext++ RGB-D provider adds value beyond fixed dense persistence. Manual material identity is used only at the query frame and for post-seal source scoring. This is not independent confirmation, a fair open-loop SOTA claim, or authority to inspect held-v8.
